solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Contributor to 10's almost in a knot…

indicators.note: in signals that the word for almost is placed inside the abbreviation

parts.note: KT is an abbreviation for a knot, the nautical unit of speed
nigh is an old word meaning almost or nearly

explanation.surface: Someone helping with a poet's work is all tied up in knots.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipses chain the first clues as a list of Chaucer's pilgrims; 10 is CHAUCER.
explanation.definitionFit: The Knight tells the first of the Canterbury Tales, so he is one of the poet's storytellers.

clue.text: …another is female, endlessly irritating…

indicators.note: endlessly says the word for irritating loses its final letter

parts.note: something rankling is irritating, galling, festering

explanation.surface: Continuing the list: this other person is a woman who is constantly annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' carries on from 1-down: another contributor to the Canterbury Tales.
explanation.definitionFit: The Franklin, a wealthy landowner, is another pilgrim who tells a tale in Chaucer's collection.

clue.text: …another put sinners out

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: And yet another person throws the wrongdoers out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' again continues the run of Chaucer's storytellers from 1-down.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nun's Priest, chaplain to the Prioress, tells the tale of Chauntecleer the cockerel in Chaucer's collection.

clue.text: Copse managed at this point where it's easy to breathe

indicators.note: a managed wood has been worked and rearranged, so the letters of copse are reordered

parts.note: at this point means here, in this place

explanation.surface: A coppiced wood is a spot of fresh air where breathing comes easily.
explanation.definitionFit: The ecosphere is the part of the planet and its atmosphere that can support life, a breathable zone.

clue.text: See 22
'Cat' commander gets a good deal, we hear

parts.note: OC stands for Officer Commanding, a military commander

indicators.note: we hear signals that the phrase for a good deal is to be taken by its sound

parts.note: a good deal means a lot

explanation.surface: An army officer nicknamed 'Cat' strikes a favourable bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: OC plus 'a lot' spoken quickly sounds like the name of the wild cat.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocelot is a spotted wild feline of the Americas, so it is a kind of cat.

clue.text: Contributor to 10 has papers about French king's ascent

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the newspapers go round the king

parts.note: the press means newspapers collectively

indicators.note: in a down clue an ascent reads the French king upwards, so backwards

parts.note: roi is French for king

explanation.surface: A Chaucer storyteller holds newspapers reporting a French monarch's rise to power.
explanation.definitionFit: The Prioress, Madame Eglantine, is one of the pilgrims who tells a tale in Chaucer's poem.

clue.text: In Bordeaux one turns right by river for nourishment

indicators.note: turns tells us the French word for one is read backwards

parts.note: un is French for one, as spoken in Bordeaux
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: In a French city someone turns right beside a river looking for food.
explanation.definitionFit: Nurture is care and feeding that helps something grow, a synonym for nourishment.

clue.text: Foil group of life peers

indicators.note: group of says a cluster of consecutive letters is taken from inside the words life peers

explanation.surface: A party of lords foils a plan.
explanation.definitionFit: The foil and the épée are both fencing swords, so each is an instance of the other's class of weapon; here foil means fencing sword.

clue.text: Poet failing to rewrite cartouche

indicators.note: failing to means the word to is absent from the letters used
rewrite asks for the remaining letters of cartouche to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A poet fails to redraft an Egyptian name-oval.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove T and O from CARTOUCHE, leaving CARUCHE, and rearrange those seven letters. A cartouche is the oval enclosing a pharaoh's name in hieroglyphs.
explanation.definitionFit: Geoffrey Chaucer was the fourteenth-century English writer of verse, author of the Canterbury Tales.

clue.text: Thugs bringing sense of foreboding into German society

indicators.note: into says the feeling of dread is placed inside the abbreviations

parts.note: angst is a feeling of dread or anxiety

explanation.surface: Hoodlums bring a sense of dread into a German club.
explanation.definitionFit: Gangsters are violent criminals in organised gangs, so thugs is a fair synonym.

clue.text: How do you do nothing after nightmare?

indicators.note: after places the zero at the end, following the bad experience

parts.note: a nightmare experience is hell
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: How do you manage with nothing left after a terrible ordeal?
explanation.definitionFit: Hello is a greeting, the same social function as the formal greeting how do you do.

clue.text: He may be busy at the wall until eryngium's pruned

definitions.text: He may be busy at the wall

indicators.note: pruned says the two words are cut back at both ends, leaving a run of inner letters

explanation.surface: A gardener at the wall keeps going until the sea holly is cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: Eryngium is sea holly, a garden plant, which steers towards gardening.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman fixing tiles is busy at walls as well as floors and roofs.

clue.text: Patron's somewhat in shade

indicators.note: in says the phrase for somewhat sits inside the word for shade

parts.note: a hue is a shade of colour
somewhat means a bit

explanation.surface: The patron is a bit in the shadows.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitué is a regular visitor to a place, a regular patron of a bar or club.

clue.text: Graduate's doodah and short gown useful in the wet?

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
a doodah is a thingummy, a thing whose name escapes you

indicators.note: short means the word for gown loses its final letter

parts.note: a cape is a sleeveless cloak, a loose outer garment like a gown

explanation.surface: A graduate's gear and robe will come in handy when it rains at the ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber swimming hat keeps the hair dry, so it is useful when swimming or in the water.

clue.text: Earliest inhabitant of Nairobi, e.g. disclosed

indicators.note: disclosed is read as dis-closed, unshut and broken open, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The first resident of the Kenyan capital, for instance, is revealed.
explanation.definitionFit: An aborigine is one of the original people living in a land, its first native inhabitant.

clue.text: Betrayals etc run wildly through 10's work

indicators.note: wildly suggests letters thrown about at random, so the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Treachery and so on runs riot through the poet's writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaucer's best-known poem is the collection of stories told by pilgrims riding to the shrine of Becket.

clue.text: Mix fuel with core from early moon

parts.note: coal is a solid fuel

indicators.note: core from says only the inside of the word for an early moon is kept, its outer letters dropped

parts.note: a crescent is the thin shape of the moon early in its cycle

explanation.surface: Blend a fuel with matter from the moon's earliest days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just joins the pieces; the middle four letters of CRESCENT are ESCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To coalesce is to combine or merge into one mass, which is what mixing does.

clue.text: Ball in reserve turned up a treat

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means the whole construction is read from the bottom upwards
in says the word for ball goes inside the word for reserve

parts.note: a pool is a reserve or common stock, as in a typing pool
a pill is a small ball, as of medicine

explanation.surface: A ball kept back produced something very nice indeed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses the whole container, not just the reserve: in a down clue the assembled letters are read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A lollipop is a sweet on a stick, a treat for a child.

clue.text: One reflecting the current situation had an audience in the morning with the Queen

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning
to have an audience with someone is to meet them, so met
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone who sums up affairs was received by the Queen one morning.
explanation.definitionFit: An ammeter measures electric current, so it reflects the state of the current flowing.

clue.text: Contributor to 10 using endless cereal crop and last of flour…

indicators.note: endless says the cereal word loses its final letter

parts.note: millet is a cereal crop grown for grain

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of flour

explanation.surface: A storyteller works with a grain crop and the remaining flour.
explanation.definitionFit: The Miller is one of Chaucer's pilgrims, and his bawdy story is among the Tales.

clue.text: As Granny to ordinance, it's relative

parts.note: Granny is NAN, and NAN sits inside the word ordinance, so Granny stands in relation to it as in
an ordinance is a law or decree

explanation.surface: A grandmother bears the same relation to a decree as to the family.
explanation.walkthrough: Granny's familiar name NAN is inside 'ordinance', and an ordinance is a law: so Granny is in law.
explanation.definitionFit: An in-law is a relative by marriage, such as a spouse's parent.

clue.text: …another's Lady Thynn?

definitions.meaning: continuing the list of Chaucer's storytellers, this is another pilgrim
the Thynn family hold the title Marquess of ...

explanation.surface: Another one belongs to a titled lady of the Thynn family.
explanation.walkthrough: The Thynns are the family of the Marquesses of Bath, at Longleat House in Wiltshire; the question mark flags the play on the title.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wife of Bath, Alisoun, is Chaucer's much-married pilgrim; a marchioness married into the Bath title is literally that.

clue.text: Reportedly 'Summoned by Bells', as were the 17ac

indicators.note: reportedly signals that a word is taken for how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: to be summoned by bells is to be tolled, as a church bell calls people

explanation.surface: John Betjeman's verse autobiography is quoted as the way the pilgrims' stories came out.
explanation.walkthrough: Summoned by Bells is John Betjeman's verse autobiography.
explanation.definitionFit: Stories are told, so the Canterbury pilgrims' tales were related or narrated.

clue.text: Regularly excels, to limits of art, gaining distinction

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter, starting with the first
limits of means the outermost letters of the word art

explanation.surface: Someone consistently excels in art, winning acclaim.
explanation.definitionFit: Éclat is brilliance or conspicuous success, so it means distinction or acclaim.

clue.text: Cutting pie

definitions.meaning: a cutting remark is sharp, sour or caustic
an open pastry case with filling, often sweet, is a kind of pie

explanation.definitionFit: Tart means sharp-tongued as an adjective, and as a noun a fruit pastry, much like a pie.

clue.text: G-g-ghastly fire — ye gods!

parts.note: G is an abbreviation for good, as on report cards

indicators.note: ghastly suggests something horribly mangled, so the letters of fire are rearranged

explanation.surface: A stammering cry at a horrible fire: heavens above!
explanation.walkthrough: The stammer gives two Gs: the first stands for GOOD, the second is kept as the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of surprise or dismay, mild oaths of the same kind.

clue.text: Mark for corporal? He's extremely vital round our Naafi, for starters

indicators.note: for starters asks for the opening letter of each of the seven words from corporal to Naafi

explanation.surface: A soldier's stripe is hugely important around the forces' canteen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporal' does double duty: it is part of the definition and also gives the first initial. The NAAFI runs canteens and shops for the British armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: A chevron is the V-shaped stripe on a sleeve showing an NCO's rank; a corporal wears two.

clue.text: Top game features a bod I trained, see?

indicators.note: trained hints at something put through its paces and reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or behold

explanation.surface: A game features a person I have coached; look at that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'features' just joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Diabolo is a juggling game in which a spinning top shaped like an hourglass is tossed on a string.
